# brevis.sh

> A data orchestration runtime written in Go. One binary holds declarative
> transformation, workflow orchestration, a persistent queue, a scheduler and an
> operational interface. Every workflow step runs as its own Kubernetes pod with
> its own image. MIT licensed.

Every page below is also served as Markdown: append `index.md` to any docs URL.
`https://brevis.sh/llms-full.txt` is this entire documentation set in one file.

How the pieces fit: a **workflow** is a YAML file of **steps**; the
**scheduler** turns schedules into **runs** and a **queue** executes them; each
step becomes a **pod**. A step is any command in any image — the **Go SDK**
(`brevis/sdk`) is for extract-and-load work, and the **client libraries**
(`pip install brevis`) give a step the run's context, clock and metrics through
two environment variables.

The same documentation in Portuguese: https://brevis.sh/docs/ (append `index.md` likewise).

## Start here

- [Introduction](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/introduction/index.md): What brevis.sh is, the problem it solves, and when it is not the right choice.
- [Installation](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/installation/index.md): How to get the binary, what it requires, and how to confirm the install is correct.
- [Quickstart](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/quickstart/index.md): From nothing to a live DAG in the interface, in four steps.

## Building a workflow

- [Workflows](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/workflows/index.md): The complete YAML format — steps, dependencies, images, resources and schedule.
- [Parameters](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/parameters/index.md): What changes between two runs of the same workflow, without editing the file.
- [Step runtime](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/runtime/index.md): What a step declares about the language and tools it drives — and why you rarely need to.
- [Context between steps](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/context/index.md): What one step tells the next — two environment variables and a file.

## How it executes

- [Scheduler and queue](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/scheduler-and-queue/index.md): Two independent loops — who creates runs, who executes them, and why they are separate.
- [Pod per step](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/pod-per-step/index.md): Why each step runs in its own pod, and what that changes in cost and isolation.

## Command line and configuration

- [CLI](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/cli/index.md): The engine's twelve subcommands, with flags, arguments and what each one requires.
- [Configuration](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/configuration/index.md): Every environment variable, with default, format and what happens when it is missing.

## Writing a step in code

- [Go SDK](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/sdk/index.md): Writing a fetcher — extract from a source, transform, and load into a destination.
- [Client libraries](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/libraries/index.md): How a step in any language reads the context and the run's clock — and which languages already have a library.
- [Python](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/python/index.md): pip install brevis — context between steps, the run's clock and your pipeline's own metrics, with no dependencies at all.

## Running it in production

- [Kubernetes](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/kubernetes/index.md): How to deploy the engine, with what permissions, and what to check afterwards.
- [Observability](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/observability/index.md): Prometheus metrics from both processes, what to watch, and what is deliberately absent.
- [White label](https://brevis.sh/en/docs/white-label/index.md): Changing the interface's title, motto, logo and palette through one YAML file.
